findings.summary: docs/system-facts.md is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The fallback for the verifier pin conflict points the wrong way: trimming the verifier frame makes run_pin_tests.rs:1618 fail sooner, not later.
findings.evidence: run_pin_tests.rs:1608-1618 needs contract + 2×VERIFIER_FRAME to be greater than BudgetSet::Verifier (left == 0). Call the contract C, the verifier frame V and the largest capability verifier section K (study). The pin needs C+2V > B, and the 90% rule needs C+V+K ≤ 0.9B. Cutting V by x lowers the pin side by 2x but the real set by only x, so the pin breaks first. Both rules hold only while 0.8V > 0.1C + K. With the plan's targets (C≈277, K≈284) that means V > about 390 tokens, and the plan targets V≈417, so the margin is about 27 tokens. 'Trim the verifier frame by a few bytes' eats that margin. Raising the budget also breaks the pin. Fix: Fix the fallback. If the pin and the 90% rule conflict, shrink the largest capability verifier section (study verifier.md) or the contract, or keep the verifier frame longer. Do not trim VERIFIER_FRAME. Add the inequality (0.8·V > 0.1·C + K) to the step 5 comment so the producer can check it before writing the files to their byte targets, and set V's byte target with that margin in mind.

findings.summary: The approach moves the severity scale into the optional doc, but the critic and verifier act on those definitions. Moved out, the scale becomes a rule that exists only in Athena's own tree.
findings.evidence: critic.md:12 and verifier.md:10 define blocker, major, minor and nit. These lines decide the verdict: accept only when no finding is blocker or major (critic.md:13), and records/plan.rs:187 enforces that rule. The CriticOutput schema gives severity only as an enum, with no descriptions. The plan's verifier entry keeps 'severity', but the critic entry does not, and the approach lists the severity scale among the items moved. The new pointer test only checks pinned phrases, and no test pins the severity definitions, so nothing would catch their removal. On any other repository the doc is missing, so the critic would grade findings with no definitions. That contradicts the plan's own invariant that the doc 'never [holds] an instruction an agent must follow'. Fix: Keep the one-line severity definitions in both critic.md and verifier.md. Remove 'severity scale' from the list of moved content; the doc may hold examples per severity only. Optionally add the severity terms to the anchors the new test checks in the frames.
findings.location: Approach ('Move explanatory knowledge (… severity scale …)'), Files: critic.md, docs/agent-reference.md

findings.summary: The criterion 4 test promises to check that 'no pinned rule lives only in the doc' but gives no mechanism.
findings.evidence: The existing wording tests (lib.rs:441-543, briefs.rs:1584-1616) each hold their own local lists of phrases. No shared list exists that the new test could iterate over, so this part of the assertion is unspecified. Fix: Have the new test read docs/agent-reference.md and assert it contains none of an explicit anchor list declared in the test (or a shared const used by the wording tests). Otherwise drop that claim from the demonstration.

findings.summary: The stale-comment fix and the bound ratchet should not cite '1300' or a fixed bound in the new comment text.
findings.evidence: The current comment at lib.rs:405 says 'each stays inside the 1300-token budget checked above'. Once the budgets drop, a new comment naming a number will go stale on the next edit, which is the same problem as the old one. Fix: Word the new comment by relation ('inside the producer and verifier budgets checked above'). Put the measured figure in the bound only.

findings.summary: The docs/system-facts.md edit is forced and correctly justified. Asking the user to confirm it adds a question with only one workable answer.
findings.evidence: budgets.rs:109-113 rejects any size or budget mismatch, so any prompt edit fails cargo test unless lines 21-26 change. Athena already raised the scope point as minor. Fix: Keep the edit. Drop the question, or state it as a notice rather than a choice.

summary: I read the code behind the plan: lib.rs (budgets, check_budget, the frame-bound and contract tests), budgets.rs (the computed rows, the facts check, every_role_set_is_within_its_budget), run_pin_tests.rs:1581-1625, the critic and verifier prompts, and the readers of the frame constants. The plan's seams exist and match the code: check_budget, compose, wiring::capabilities(), the *_FRAME constants and the computed facts rows. Its dependents list covers every reader I found by grepping for the frame texts and BudgetSet::Producer and Verifier. The forced edit to docs/system-facts.md is correctly argued. The optional, conditional reference doc is a reasonable answer to the round-one finding. Two soundness problems remain. First, the fallback for the verifier pin conflict runs the wrong way. The pin needs contract + 2 × verifier frame > budget, so trimming the frame breaks the pin first. The real levers are the study verifier section or the contract, and the margin is only about 27 tokens by estimate. Second, the approach moves the severity scale into a doc that exists only in Athena's own tree. The critic and verifier need those definitions to set their verdict, and no test pins them, so the plan would break its own rule that the doc holds no instruction an agent needs to act. Both are fixable in the plan, so the verdict is revise.
